newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland still confident on 1997 EMU deficit.
newsitem.headline: Finland still confident on 1997 EMU deficit.

text.p: HELSINKI, July 28 (Reuteor) - The Finnish finance ministry said on Monday the public sector deficit in relation to gross domestic product (GDP) would be inside the three-percent limit goal for European economic and monetary union (EMU) despite an overshoot to 3.1 percent in 1996.
Even in a worst-case scenario, the 1997 deficit would be safely within the EMU limit, state secretary Raimo Sailas told Reuters by telephone.

"We have not changed our forecast for this year," Sailas said, referring to the ministry's deficit forecast of 1.4 percent of GDP. Countries aiming to join the single currency will be judged by their 1997 performance.
Sailas and an official at Statistics Finland (SF) attributed a recent revision of the 1996 deficit to 3.1 percent of GDP from 2.6 percent mainly to non-recurring factors.
Earlier this month in Brussels, data showed a statistical revision pushing Finland's 1996 deficit above the EMU limit.

The revised deficit was slightly more than three billion markka ($550.2 million) higher, mainly because late 1996 state expenditure was underestimated in SF's preliminary figures released on March 3, the SF official said.
Asked if there was any reason to expect revisions next year of preliminary 1997 data to push Finland's public sector deficit over the three-percent EMU goal, Sailas said "the answer is no."
"We have made test calculations, and we will be safely below three percent even in a worst-case scenario," he said.

Since public sector finance data for all European Union (EU) countries will still be preliminary in spring 1998 and subject to many later revisions, heated debate in many EU countries on the EMU deficit criterion, especially on minutiae like decimals, was rather pointless, Sailas said.
EU leaders are scheduled to decide in April-May 1998 which countries qualify for the planned third stage of the single currency due to start in 1999.
Finland has repeatedly said it will meet the entry criteria and intends to be among the founders of the new euro.
